newsitem.title: JAPAN: HK governor Patten begins six-day Japan visit.
newsitem.headline: HK governor Patten begins six-day Japan visit.

text.p: Hong Kong governor Chris Patten arrived here on Tuesday for a six-day visit to foster closer economic and trade ties between the British colony and Japan.

Patten is to attend the 19th joint session of the Japan-Hong Kong and Hong Kong-Japan economic committees and meet Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda and Trade Minister Shinji Sato.

He will also meet political leaders including Ichiro Ozawa who heads the main opposition Shinshinto (New Frontier Party). Patten was expected to discuss with Japanese leaders the British colony's future before and after its handover to China next year, Japanese officials said.
More than 150 years of British colonial rule will end at midnight next June 30 when Hong Kong reverts to China as a Special Administrative Region (SAR).
Before leaving Hong Kong on Tuesday, Patten said he would press Tokyo to grant Hong Kong people visa-free entry after the British colony reverts back to China.
Patten said he would try to persuade Japan to afford Hong Kong's post-1997 passports preferential treatment over mainland Chinese passports.
So far only Britain, Singapore and Western Samoa have promised SAR passport holders visa-free entry.
